=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- .claude/hooks/gh_api_write_guard.py:1160-1164 | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: `_approved_echo_read_command` rejects `$` characters inside single-quoted jq programs, even though they are literal text and do not undergo shell expansion.
  WHY: This incorrectly rejects valid read-only substitutions; severity was consistently reported as NIT.
- .claude/hooks/gh_api_write_guard.py:line 1325 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: The hidden-call ask path adds `_ECHO_READ_HINT` only when the command contains `"$("`, omitting the approved-loop rewrite hint for unapproved loop variants without that text.
  WHY: Such loops receive only the generic ask message instead of the rewrite guidance; minimax rated this MAJOR while the other reviewers rated it NIT.
- .claude/hooks/gh_api_write_guard.py:1370-1374 | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The write-reason path appends `_ECHO_READ_HINT` to loop-write asks, although the hint tells the caller to run the call separately “For reads”.
  WHY: The hint is misleading for a legitimate write and its suggested read shape would not accomplish that write; severity was consistently reported as NIT.
- tests/test_gh_api_write_guard.py:771-772 | severity=low | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: `test_unsafe_echo_substitution_is_not_allowed` asserts only that the decision is not `DECISION_ALLOW`, rather than requiring `DECISION_ASK`.
  WHY: The test would pass for `None` or `DECISION_DENY`, so it does not enforce the required ask outcome.
- changelog.d/4909-guard-echo-read-substitutions.md:lines 1-2 | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The changelog fragment contains only a headline and omits the lead paragraph and audience closing required by §20.D.
  WHY: The release notes will lack the operator impact and audience takeaway required by the documented changelog structure.

=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- .claude/hooks/gh_api_write_guard.py:line 1325 | severity=low | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The `_ECHO_READ_HINT` condition on the hidden-call ask path checks only `"$(" in command`, unlike the parse-error path (line 1318) and shell-rewrite-hazard path (line 1365) which additionally check `_LOOP_HEADER_RE.match(command)`. A loop without a dollar-paren substitution (e.g., using backticks or an executor) that triggers `has_hidden_gh_api` receives the generic denial without the approved-loop rewrite hint that the issue decision requires.
  WHY: An interactive session running an unapproved loop variation sees no suggestion and waits at the prompt instead of retrying the approved shape.
- .claude/hooks/gh_api_write_guard.py:line 1163 | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: `normalized_body = body if "$" not in body else None` rejects any `$` in the substitution body, even a literal `$` inside single quotes (e.g., `--jq '.["$"]'`) that the shell never expands.
  WHY: A valid echo-read command with a literal `$` in a single-quoted jq expression is rejected. This is fail-closed so no security risk, but it is inconsistent with the loop path which correctly distinguishes single-quoted from expandable characters via `_substitute_loop_var`.
- .claude/hooks/gh_api_write_guard.py:line 1372 | severity=low | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The hint text begins "For reads, run the call separately, e.g. ..." but line 1372 appends it when a loop contains a write (the for-loop header matches but contents are writes).
  WHY: A session denied for a loop containing writes may try to follow the hint and reshape into a read-only form, which would not accomplish the intended write operation.
- tests/test_gh_api_write_guard.py:lines 771-772 | severity=low | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The assertion checks only `!= guard.DECISION_ALLOW`, not `== guard.DECISION_ASK`.
  WHY: The test does not prove the guard asks on those commands. A future change that silently returns no-decision for one of these cases would not be caught.
- Requirement: "§23.H stays authoritative. Update its table and §23.D.4's wording in CLAUDE.md and workflow-templates/CLAUDE.md byte for byte."
  Expected change site: CLAUDE.md §23.H table (lines 1318-1323) and §23.D.4 (lines 1204-1208); workflow-templates/CLAUDE.md is a symlink to ../CLAUDE.md so it is covered.
  Evidence of absence: The PR diff contains no changes to CLAUDE.md. The §23.H read row mentions only literal-ID loop approval, not the new echo-of-read-substitution acceptance. The §23.H write row still says "in a backtick or double-quoted $(...) substitution Bash would run" is always a write — but _approved_echo_read_command now allows some $(...) REST reads in echo arguments. The §23.H decision paragraph (lines 1325-1354) describes the loop exception but not the echo-substitution exception. §23.D.4 (line 1207) says "Except for the literal-ID read loops in §23.H, keep gh api calls out of loops, $(...)" with no mention of the echo-read exception. The hook docstring and agents.md were updated, but CLAUDE.md — the authoritative §23.H section the issue names — was not.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- Requirement: "A changelog.d/ fragment (§20)."
  Expected change site: changelog.d/4909-guard-echo-read-substitutions.md
  Evidence of absence: The fragment delivers only the headline sentence (2 lines). CLAUDE.md §20.D requires a lead paragraph of 3-5 sentences on operator impact, and an audience closing paragraph. The fragment omits the structured body the assembler expects.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- .claude/hooks/gh_api_write_guard.py:line 1325 (the hidden-call branch in evaluate, `+ (_ECHO_READ_HINT if "$(" in command else "")`) | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The hint condition is inconsistent with the sibling paths (lines 1318 and 1365), which both check `"$(" in command or _LOOP_HEADER_RE.match(command)`. A hidden call that lives inside a loop frame but does not contain `$(...)` text — e.g. `for n in 1 2; do echo `gh api ...`; done` (backtick substitution) or `for n in 1 2; do bash -c "gh api ..."; done` (executor) — reaches this branch and never receives the issue's required safe-rewrite suggestion. The fix is to mirror the sibling condition: `if "$(" in command or _LOOP_HEADER_RE.match(command)`.
  WHY: an interactive session that trips an ASK through a hidden call inside a loop will see only the generic "Run it as its own plain command" message instead of the `for n in …; do echo $n; gh api …` example the issue requires.
- .claude/hooks/gh_api_write_guard.py:lines 1162-1163 | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: For commands without a loop header the function rejects any `$` in the substitution body, including `$` characters that sit inside single quotes and are therefore literal text to Bash. The loop branch (line 1161, `_substitute_loop_var`) handles single-quoted text correctly, but the non-loop branch is more conservative than necessary.
  WHY: A session that writes `echo "$(gh api repos/o/r/issues/1 --jq '.[\"$user\"]')"` — a valid read whose jq filter holds a l
